ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text:
How much should you bet?
Most bettors guess. Kelly gives you a formula.
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text:
The common mistake: flat-betting everything the same size regardless of edge.
A 258 bps edge and a 40 bps edge are not the same bet. Treating them that way costs you long-term.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text:
Kelly sizes your bet based on two things: your estimated win probability and the odds you're getting.
More edge, more size. Less edge, less size. The formula does the math so emotion doesn't.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text:
Example: you estimate 56% win probability on a -110 line.
Full Kelly says bet about 6.4% of your bankroll.
Most serious bettors use quarter-Kelly (1.6%) to reduce variance without abandoning the logic.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text:
You don't need to run Kelly on every bet. But understanding it changes how you think about sizing.
Edge without proper sizing is a slow leak.
